title: Mass spectrometry of plasma extracellular vesicles before and after exercise
projectDescription: We aimed to identify changes in the proteome of extracellular vesicles released into circulation by 7 recreationally active endurance running-trained healthy females after a bout of 60-min incremental treadmill exercise. Blood samples were collected immediately before and after exercise and extracellular vesicles were isolated from plasma by size exclusion chromatography. The samples were then analyzed by mass spectrometry proteomics.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Sample collection and plasma isolation Blood samples were collected using BD Vacutainer® EDTA Tubes from vein before and immediately after the physical activity and kept in a thermal bag until plasma isolation. Plasma samples were obtain-ing by centrifugation of blood at 1500 rpm for 10 min at 4˚C. The isolated plasma was then placed in a fresh tube and centrifuged again at 1500 rpm for 10 min at 4˚C. Finally, the obtained plasma was ali-quoted in 1.5ml Protein-Low bind Eppendorf tubes, 1 ml per aliquot, and stored frozen at -80˚C until further use.  Size Exclusion Chromatography SEC EV were isolated with qEVoriginal / 35 nm Gen 2  iZON colums using 1 ml of plasma sample per co-lumn and autoclaved PBS-DEPC filtered with a  0.2 μm filter. Briefly, the plasma was thawed in a  +37˚C water bath for 3 min and then centrifuged 10 min at 10 000 g to remove  cellular debris. The SEC columns were then washed with 10 ml of  PBS-DEPC and then 1 ml of plasma was added. The flowthrough was collected in a 1.5 ml eppendorf and then 15 fractions were collected. The isolated fractions were next measured with ZetaSizer to determine the fractions that contained EVs. EV fractions were then concentrated using Amicon Ultra-0.5, Ultracell-3 Membrane, 3 kDa filters. EVs were then aliquoted and frozen at -80˚C until further use.  In-solution digestion EVs were precipitated by incubating the samples with four times the sample volume of ice cold acetone overnight at -20°C. Samples were centrifuged at 13,000 xg at 4°C for 20 min, and the pellets were vac-uum dried to remove traces of acetone before being dissolved in 50 µl 6 M urea in 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate and reduced with 5 mM dithiotreitol at 30°C for 30 min. Exposed side chains were alkylat-ed by incubation with 25 mM iodoacetamide for1 h at room temperature protected from light. The samples were further reduced with 50 mM DTT at 30°C  for 30 min. The enzymatic digestion was per-formed by adding 2 µg trypsine in 240 ul 50mM ammonium bicarbonate to the samples and incubating them overnight at 37°C. Prior to LC-MS/MS analysis, the obtained peptides were desalted by reversed-phase chromatography using OMIX C18 filter tips. Peptides were eluted by applying 80% acetonitrile in 0.1% formic acid. Acetonitrile was evaporated in a vacuum drier and the volume was adjusted by adding 0.1% formic acid.  Mass spectrometric analyses Samples were analyzed on a timsTOF pro interfaced with a Nanoelute (Bruker). Peptides were separat-ed on a 25-cm bed length Aurora column (C18, 1.7 μm, 120 Å, 75 μm inner diameter) with column temperature 50°C and a flow rate of 300 nl/min. Solvent A was water with 0.1% formic acid and sol-vent B was acetonitrile with 0.1% formic acid. A 60 min gradient from 2% to 35% solvent B was used for separation. The mass spectrometer was operated in a data-dependent acquisition mode with auto-matic switching between MS and MS/MS. The m/z range for full MS went from 100 to 1700. The TIMS range started at 0.85 1/K0 and finished at 1.4 1/K0, with a ramp time and accumulation time of 100ms and a 100% duty cycle. MS/MS spectra were acquired for the ten most abundant ions (Top10 method). MS/MS scans were acquired using 10 PASEF ramps, with a total cycle time of 1.16 seconds. Precursor target intensity was set to 20000, with an intensity threshold of 1750. Collisions energies ranges from 0.6 ev (at 0.6 1/K0) to 1.6 eV (at 1.6 1/K0).
dataProcessingProtocol: The software PEAKS studio version 10.6 (Bioinformatics Solutions inc., Ontario, Canada) was used for protein identification, label-free quantitation and statistical analysis. MS and MS/MS spectra were searched against the UniProtKB FASTA database for the human proteome (85,915 entries including isoforms and canonical sequences; downloaded from http://www.UniProt.org, 2019). The following parameters were applied: enzyme: trypsin with no proline restriction; variable modifications: oxidation, acetylation (protein N-term), fixed modification: carbamidomethyl (C). The first search was performed with mass tolerance of 15 ppm for the precursor ion, and mass tolerance for fragment ions was set to 0.03 Dalton . Minimal unique peptides were set to 1, and a false-discovery rate of 0.01 was used in all instances. Protein significance was determined with the in-build PEAKS analysis module, using an ANOVA test with a 0.05 adjusted p-value threshold.
